intervals.label: Boulby Underground Laboratory operating
intervals.note: The official STFC/Boulby timeline's earliest dated entry is 'first radioactive background measurements taken underground in Boulby Mine' (1989); this marks the start of scientific use rather than a separately-stated formal-establishment date, but the laboratory has operated continuously since and is described as currently active on the fetched official page, so status is recorded as active rather than as a discrete commissioning phase.
intervals.quote: first radioactive background measurements taken underground in Boulby Mine

operator_text.quote: Operated by STFC in close partnership with ICL-UK
operator_text.value: STFC (Science and Technology Facilities Council), in close partnership with ICL-UK

summary.plain: A deep underground science laboratory in a working mine on the English coast, more than a kilometre below ground. It hosts dark-matter searches and other experiments that need to be shielded from cosmic rays.
summary.technical: UK STFC underground laboratory hosted within the ICL-UK (formerly Cleveland Potash) mine near Boulby, North Yorkshire, at ~1.1 km depth beneath the North York Moors.
